They eat fruit, honey and fish.

dialog.g: In the forest there are … . A bear is … than a wolf. In the forest we should … .

gaplar.g: Is it hot or cold in the desert?
The Kyzylkum is a big desert in Uzbekistan.
There is sand everywhere in the desert.
The desert is very hot and dry.
A camel can live in the desert.
It can go many days without water.
Forty years ago I worked there.
There were camels, snakes and tortoises.

dialog.g: Grandpa, were you in the Kyzylkum?
Yes, I was. Forty years ago I worked there.
Was it hot?
Very hot and dry! There was sand everywhere.
Were there animals?
Yes, there were. There were camels, snakes and tortoises.

gaplar.g: There is no sea near Tashkent.
But last summer Nigora was at the sea!
The sea is bigger than a lake.
There is a small island in the middle of the lake.
A ship is bigger than a boat.
Last summer Nigora and her family were at the sea.
The water was warm and blue.
Nigora played in the waves with her brother.
One day they were on a big ship.
It stopped at a small island.
The Fergana Valley is between the mountains.
Farmers grow cotton and wheat in the fields.
There are apple and peach orchards in the valley.
There is a beautiful waterfall in the mountains.
The water is cold and fresh.
Let's describe nature with there is and there are.
My dad grows wheat and cotton.
The water is very cold, but it's beautiful.
Tell the class about it with there is / there are.
Water comes down from the top of a high rock.

dialog.g: Dilnoza, your valley is very green!
Yes. There are many fields here. My dad grows wheat and cotton.
Are there mountains near here?
Yes, all around the valley. There is a waterfall too. Let's walk there tomorrow!
Is it far?
No, it's near. The water is very cold, but it's beautiful.

gaplar.g: This time they were in the mountains.
From the top of the hill there is a beautiful view.
Last Sunday Grade 5 was on a trip to Chimgan.
The morning was cool and sunny.
The children walked up a high hill.
Timur was faster than everybody, but Madina was more careful.
«This view is more beautiful than a picture!» Nigora smiled.
In the evening the children were tired, but very happy.
Find these words in the story.
Tell the story to your classmate.
Then talk about a trip of your class.
There is snow on the top.
Make a poster Make a poster «The nature of Uzbekistan».
Write five sentences with there is / there are and one comparison.

dialog.g: What can tourists see in Uzbekistan?
There are high mountains near Tashkent. There is snow on the top.
There is a big desert, the Kyzylkum. There are camels there.
There are rivers and lakes. Lake Charvak is very deep.
And there are green fields in the Fergana Valley!
Great! Our country is very beautiful.

gaplar.g: The school year is almost over!
Units 5–8 Jobs, health, countries and nature.
In September we were on a trip to Samarkand.
In winter we played in the snow.
In spring Lola was ill, but Grandma's soup helped her.
Lola's pen friend Emma is from England.
Now we know about many countries and the nature of Uzbekistan.
We are older and cleverer than last year!
There are games, songs and a little play.
Favourite words What are your favourite words from Grade 5?
Here are some from the class.
I was slower, but I never stopped.
A slow and careful tortoise is healthier than a fast rabbit!
Act out the little play in groups of four.

dialog.g: rocket, pilot, faster
artist, feather, view
elephant, firefighter, camel
kitten, pen friend, honey
Good morning! What's the matter? Rabbit
I was in a race yesterday. I jumped and jumped. Now I've got a backache! Doctor
Oh dear! You should rest. And you, Mr Tortoise? Tortoise
I'm fine! I was slower, but I never stopped. I was first! Doctor

gaplar.g: Where were you in the summer?
Ali has a story about his summer.
Last summer I was in the mountains near Chimgan with my family.
The weather was sunny and the river was cold and fast.
Every morning I walked to the river with my dad.
We played football in the field and cooked plov.
One day I was very tired.
We talk about yesterday and last summer.
Last Saturday Ali went to his grandma's house.
There are cows, sheep and hens.
In the evening Ali's dad came to grandma's house too.
On Sunday Ali came back home.

dialog.g: Where were you on Sunday, Ali?
I went to my grandma's village.
Was it fun?
Yes! I walked by the river and helped grandpa in the garden.
And now you are back at school!
Yes, we came back last night.

gaplar.g: The lion is big and strong.
It has got a long tail.
Last Sunday Madina went to the zoo.
She saw a lion and two monkeys.

dialog.g: Mum, look! I saw a lion!
Yes, it's very big. And there are the monkeys.
They ate all the bananas!
They were hungry. Are you hungry too?
No, I ate an ice cream. Thank you, Mum!
I saw a … . It ate … .

gaplar.g: Is it sunny or rainy today?
What do you take to school on a rainy day?
Lola took her umbrella to school.
Timur took a photo of the rain.
In the evening Lola and her mum made a cake.
And I made a cake yesterday.

dialog.g: Lola, you took your umbrella. Good!
Yes, it was rainy in the morning.
I took a photo of the rain. Look!
Nice photo! And I made a cake yesterday. Here you are.
Mmm, yummy! Thank you!

gaplar.g: This is the key to my house.
His sister found the key under the sofa.
Nigora found a small puppy in the street.
Last Monday Nigora went to the shop.
What do you do at a party?
Last Friday Timur had a birthday party.
After the cake the children ran into the garden and played.
I had a very happy day!
Now we know twelve special verbs!

dialog.g: How was the party, Timur?
Great! I had a very happy day!
What is this book?
Lola gave it to me. It's about animals.
And your friends?
They said 'Happy birthday!' Then we ran and played in the garden.

gaplar.g: It's from Aziz to his grandma in Khiva.
Aziz wrote the letter last night.
In the morning he drank tea with milk and went to school.
Last night the baby slept well.
Last week we went to the mountains.
We saw a big river and ate plov near it.
I drank cold water from the river.

dialog.g: went, ate, drank, slept.

gaplar.g: Today's story is about a monkey and Timur's hat!
Everybody in our class likes English.
Last Saturday Timur and his family went to the zoo.
Then they came to the monkeys.
Suddenly a little monkey ran to him and took his hat!
Then it climbed a tree and put the hat on its head.
On Saturday I went to the shop with Mum.
But my puppy found it in the garden.
Write five sentences about last week.
Lola's key was in the garden.

dialog.g: Lola, how was your weekend?
Great! On Saturday I went to the shop with Mum. We made samsa.
Yummy! And on Sunday?
I lost my key! But my puppy found it in the garden.
Ha-ha! A clever puppy!
Yes! I gave him milk.

gaplar.g: What film did you see last?
There is a big cinema in our city.
Last Sunday Lola went to the cinema.
The film was about a lion.

dialog.g: Did you go to the cinema yesterday, Madina?
Yes, I did. I went with my sister.
Did you like the film?
Yes, I did! It was very funny.
Did you eat popcorn?
No, I didn't. I drank juice.
yes or no.

gaplar.g: Chorsu is a big bazaar in Tashkent.
On Saturday Dad went to the bazaar.
When did Dad go to the bazaar?

dialog.g: Timur, when did Dad buy the meat?
He bought it in the morning.
Did he buy onions too?
No, he didn't. We didn't see good onions.
OK. When did you come back?
We came back at ten. Then Dad went to work.

gaplar.g: Do you watch football on TV?
Yesterday there was a football match at school.

dialog.g: Hello, Ali! Who won the match?
We won, Dad! Three — one!
Well done! Who scored the goals?
Aziz scored two goals and I scored one.
Great! What did your teacher say?
She said: 'Well done, boys!'
Who opened the window?

gaplar.g: Today Aziz woke up very late — at half past seven!
He forgot his English book at home.
He was late because he woke up late.
He was sad because he forgot his book.
My baby brother cried all night.

dialog.g: Aziz, why are you late?
Sorry, I woke up late.
Why did you wake up late?
Because I didn't sleep well. My baby brother cried all night.
I see. Where is your book?
Oh no! I forgot it at home!

gaplar.g: How do you come to school?
Yesterday it was rainy, so Lola went to school by taxi.
The film was very long and boring.

dialog.g: Madina, how was your weekend?
It was wonderful! We went to Samarkand.
How did you go there?
By car. In the old city we walked on foot.
Was it a long day?
Yes. Five hours in the car was boring. But Registan was beautiful!

gaplar.g: There is something on the floor.
Grandma has a beautiful blue vase.
The cat is sleeping on the floor.
Madina told her mum the truth.

dialog.g: Who broke the vase?
I didn't break it! I was in the garden.
Madina, where were you? What did you do?
I was in the kitchen. I made tea.
Then why is the cat on the table?
Oh! The cat broke it! Look, it ran to the garden!
Thank you, Madina. You told me the truth.
broke, floor, ran, told.

gaplar.g: When did you see it last?
Is my bag at your house?
I stopped in the park and played chess with Grandpa Karim!
Find the questions in the story.

dialog.g: Mum, I can't find my school bag!
Don't be worried. When did you see it last?
Yesterday afternoon. I came home on foot.
Did you take it to Ali's house?
Yes, I did! We did our homework there.
Then call Ali!
Hello, Ali! Is my bag at your house?
No, it isn't. You took it.

gaplar.g: Who can ask a good question about yesterday?
Why didn't you come to school today?
Did you go to the doctor?
Mum and I went by taxi.
Write five questions to your favourite footballer about his or her last weekend.
Why did you take a taxi?

dialog.g: Hi, Madina! Why didn't you come to school today?
Because I had a cold. I stayed at home.
Oh no! Did you go to the doctor?
Yes, I did. Mum and I went by taxi.
What did the doctor say?
She said: 'Drink warm tea and rest.'
Did you …?

gaplar.g: There is a list for the weekend.
Lola has a plan for the weekend.
She wrote it in her notebook.
Tomorrow Lola is going to visit her grandma.
Next week Lola is going to play in a chess match.

dialog.g: Lola, what are you going to do tomorrow?
I'm going to visit my grandma. We're going to make samsa.
Yummy! And on Sunday?
I'm going to do my homework. What about you?
My dad and I are going to watch the football match.
Great plan!

gaplar.g: Uzbek, Russian and English are languages.
Madina is going to learn French.
He wants to play the guitar.
Timur is going to start guitar lessons next week.
When are you going to start?

dialog.g: Timur, what are you going to learn this year?
I'm going to learn the guitar.
Cool! When are you going to start?
Next week. And you?
I'm going to learn a new language — French.
Bonjour! That's 'hello' in French!

gaplar.g: Where do people like to go in the summer?
Last year we went to Bukhara.

dialog.g: Aziz, are you going to travel this summer?
Yes, I am! We're going to visit my aunt in Khiva.
Is your cousin going to be there?
Yes, she is. Her name is Dilnoza.
Are you going to swim in the Amu Darya?
No, I'm not. The river is very fast!
This is my aunt. Her name is … .

gaplar.g: It's a good day to eat outside!
On Sunday our class is going to have a picnic in the park.
Lola is going to invite her friends to the picnic.
Ali is going to bring apples and water.
We're going to sit on a big blanket under the trees.
Yes or no to the plan.
Who is going to bring what?

dialog.g: Let's have a picnic on Sunday! I'm going to invite everybody.
Great! I'm going to bring apples.
I'm going to bring a blanket.
I'm not going to bring cake. My mum is busy.
That's OK. I'm going to make sandwiches.
What a wonderful plan!

gaplar.g: The picnic is in the park.
But what is in the sky?
There's going to be a storm!
We can see it now — it's going to happen!

dialog.g: Look at the sky! It's very black.
Oh no! It's going to rain.
There's going to be a storm! Let's go home.
Be careful, Lola! The grass is wet.
Thanks! Madina, take the blanket!
OK! Run, everybody! We're going to be wet!

gaplar.g: What do you want to be?
Nigora's dream is a big library in her village.
Aziz is going to become a pilot.
Next month there is going to be a chess competition in Tashkent.
Madina won the first prize in the English competition!
She loves English and she reads English books every evening.
Lola and Ali have got a plan.
We're going to make a surprise for her.
What are we going to do?
You're going to draw a big card.
The next day Lola got up early.
She made a cake with Dad.
Ali drew a card with red flowers.
In the evening Aunt Malika came.

dialog.g: Ali, Mum's birthday is tomorrow. Let's make a surprise!
Great! What are we going to do?
I'm going to make a cake. You're going to draw a big card.
And Dad is going to bring flowers.
We're going to invite Aunt Malika too.
Shh! Mum is coming!
We're going to … .

gaplar.g: What are you going to do after school today?
One pupil is going to get a prize.
I'm going to read English stories.
Plan a class trip in groups.
Where are you going to go?
How are you going to travel?
What are you going to bring?

dialog.g: Children, next week we are going to have a competition.
What competition?
An English competition. One pupil is going to get a prize.
I'm going to learn twenty new words!
I'm not going to watch TV. I'm going to read English stories.
Great plans! Good luck!

gaplar.g: But we can think about it!
In the future people will live on Mars.
In the future cars won't need drivers.
Maybe robots will cook dinner for us.
A plan or what we think?

dialog.g: I'm going to visit Grandma tomorrow. We think: People will live on Mars.
Cars won't need drivers.
What will life be like in the future?
I think people will live on Mars.
Maybe! And cars will fly.
Children won't go to school. They'll learn at home with robots.
Oh no! I like school. I'll miss my friends!
Don't worry. Maybe robots will be our friends too!

gaplar.g: What can you see in the sky?
Would you like to go there?
The Moon and the stars are in space.
A rocket can fly into space.
People will probably fly to the Moon in the future.
There will probably be more parks.
He has a small telescope and he watches the stars every night.
'In the future people will probably fly to Mars by rocket,' he says.

dialog.g: In the future we will fly to … .

gaplar.g: Grandma has got three heavy bags.
I'll carry them for you, Grandma.
Don't worry, I'll lend you my pen.
I promise I'll clean my room tomorrow.

dialog.g: Hurry up, Timur! It's half past seven.
I can't find my English book!
Don't worry. I'll lend you my book.
And this bag is heavy.
I'll carry it, Mum.
Thank you! Will you come home early today?
Yes, I promise. I won't be late!

gaplar.g: Do you watch the weather on TV in the evening?
Tomorrow it will be hot in Termez — forty degrees!
In the morning it will be foggy.
After the rain there will be a rainbow.
Here is the weather forecast for tomorrow.
In Tashkent it will be sunny and warm — twenty-five degrees.
In Samarkand it will be cloudy in the morning, but it won't rain.
In Nukus it will be windy.
In the mountains near Chimgan it will be foggy and cold — only five degrees.
There are desks, chairs and a board.
There is a computer in our school library.
In the future every desk will have a screen.
Press the button and the robot will open the door.
A robot can't laugh at our jokes!
Draw the classroom of the future.
Will there be a school bus?

dialog.g: Aziz, what will our school be like in 2060?
There will be a smart screen on every desk.
Will there be books?
No, there won't. We'll read on computers.
Will there be teachers?
Yes, there will! A robot can't laugh at our jokes!

gaplar.g: I'm sure Lola will win the competition.
In the story the farmer found a big box of money and became rich.
Timur, I can see your future!
But you'll be a great teacher!

dialog.g: Hmm… Timur, I can see your future!
Will I be rich?
I'm sure you'll be rich. You'll have a big house.
Will I become a great footballer?
I don't think so. But you'll be a great teacher!
That's a good idea! Can you guess my name? Ha-ha!
Will I travel? Will I be rich? Will I live in a big city?

gaplar.g: What will robots do in the future?
Will they help us at home?
The books are on the shelf and the toys are in the box.
One night Aziz had a dream.
There was a robot in his room.
I'll do your homework!' Aziz was happy.

dialog.g: Aziz, look at your room! It isn't tidy.
Sorry, Mum. I'll tidy it now.
And what are you going to do after school?
I'm going to do my homework. Then I'm going to play chess with Ali.
Good. Will you help me in the kitchen too?
Yes, I will. I promise!
In 2070 robots will help us.

gaplar.g: Life is not the same now.
Robots cook and tidy the rooms.
Children learn on big screens, but there are still teachers.
Next week I'm going to fly to the Moon with my cousin.
I'm sure it will be wonderful!
One tells the forecast for tomorrow, the other draws it on the board.
Half of the year is over!
Nigora and her cousin went to the bazaar.
They bought meat and carrots, and in the evening they made plov with Grandma.
She is writing a letter to her aunt.
Tomorrow she is going to visit her uncle in the village.
The forecast says it will be sunny.
'It will be a wonderful day!' she says.

dialog.g: I'm going to visit my cousin. Look! It's going to rain.
People will live on Mars.
I'll help you!
she went / she bought / she made
she is writing
she is going to visit / it will be sunny
went, saw, Did you…?
going to, will. Your English is very good now!

gaplar.g: There are countries, mountains, rivers and seas.
There are about two hundred countries in the world.
But Tashkent is the biggest city in Uzbekistan.
Aziz is the tallest boy in our class.
The Tashkent TV Tower is very tall.
It's three hundred and seventy-five metres!

dialog.g: Who is the tallest in your family, Lola?
My dad is. He's one metre ninety!
And what is the biggest animal in your house?
Our dog Bars. He's bigger than me!
My cat is small, but she is very clever!
Ha-ha! Good, Ali!

gaplar.g: There are eleven players in a football team.
He is the best player in our team.
I'm the worst singer in my family!

dialog.g: the goodest, the baddest
Who was the best singer at the concert?
Madina! She sang an Uzbek song. It was beautiful.
And who was the worst?
Me! I forgot the words!
Ha-ha! But you are the best football player in our class.
Thank you! Football is better than singing for me.

gaplar.g: People from all over the world come to see them.
People from all over the world know it.
It is more than two thousand years old.
The Kalon Minaret in Bukhara is about forty-eight metres high.
For me, Samarkand is the most beautiful city in Uzbekistan.
Khiva is an ancient city in the west of Uzbekistan.
It has old walls and tall minarets.
The Islam Khoja Minaret is the tallest minaret in Khiva.
Bukhara is famous for the Kalon Minaret.
The best sportsmen are in the book of world records!
In 2009 Usain Bolt ran one hundred metres in 9.58 seconds.
The cheetah is the fastest animal on land.
It can run at about one hundred kilometres an hour!
The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
It's the smallest animal in my garden.

dialog.g: Today we're going to find our class records!
I'm the fastest! I ran sixty metres in nine seconds.
My hair is the longest in the class.
And I have the smallest pencil. Look!
Ha-ha! Who can write the longest English word?
Me! 'Wonderful'!
the fastest runner, the longest name, the smallest bag.

gaplar.g: Football is a popular sport in Uzbekistan.
Don't swim in a fast river.
This book about space is very interesting.
I read it in two days.
We asked twenty pupils in our class.
Plov is the most popular food — twelve pupils like it the best.
He is the oldest person in our family.
My baby brother is one year old.
A whale lives in the sea.
The blue whale is the heaviest animal in the world.

dialog.g: Nigora, how many brothers and sisters have you got?
Two brothers and one sister. I'm the oldest!
Who is the youngest?
My sister Asal. She's three.
And your brothers?
Javlon is ten and Bek is seven. Javlon is taller than me, but I'm older!

gaplar.g: Do you like quiz games on TV?
Today our class has a quiz too!
On Friday there was a big English quiz at our school.
The winner of the quiz got a prize — a book about the world.
Timur's team had eight points and Lola's team had seven.
'The winners are Timur, Madina and Nigora!' said the teacher.
All the 'top' words in the quiz.

dialog.g: Question one: What is the highest mountain in the world?
Everest!
Right! Question two: What is the fastest animal on land?
The lion?
No, sorry. Timur?
The cheetah!
Right! One point for Timur's team.

gaplar.g: Who is the best English pupil?
Tashkent is the biggest city in Uzbekistan.
Samarkand and Bukhara are among the oldest cities in the world.
Tourists think Registan is the most beautiful place in Central Asia.
The highest mountain in Uzbekistan is about four thousand six hundred metres high.
The next pupil changes one word.
Write five sentences about the records of your city or village.
Mum wants to make a cake.
We need flour for bread and cakes.
There is some flour in the box.

dialog.g: Lola, let's make a cake. Is there any flour?
Yes, there is some flour in the box.
Good. Are there any eggs?
Yes, there are some eggs on the table.
And is there any sugar?
Oh no! There isn't any sugar. I'll go to the shop!

gaplar.g: But what do we need to cook it?
First, Dad puts some oil in the pot.
We cook plov in a big pot — a kazan.
First he put some oil in the big pot.
Then he put in some meat and onions.
Then he put in some rice and some water.
Put two spoons of sugar in the tea.
Grandma gave me a bowl of soup.

dialog.g: Grandpa, how much sugar do you want in your tea?
Two spoons, please.
How many eggs do you want?
Only one. I'm not very hungry.
Here is a bowl of porridge too.
Thank you, Madina! You're the best!

gaplar.g: What do you eat for breakfast?
I put butter on my bread.
There is a lot of honey in this pot.
Grandpa has a lot of bees!
Every summer Ali goes to his grandma's village.
There is a lot of fresh bread, a lot of butter and white cheese.
Pour some oil on the salad.
Write a recipe for your favourite salad or sandwich.

dialog.g: Nigora, let's make shakarob. First, wash the tomatoes.
OK! Now can I cut them?
Yes, but be careful with the knife.
Do we add any onions?
Yes, a lot of onions! And some salt.
Can I pour some oil?
No, we don't need any oil for shakarob.

gaplar.g: Let's go to the shop with her.
Grandma has three jars of honey.
We need a packet of sugar and a packet of tea.
Two kilos of rice and one kilo of meat, please.
Two kilos of rice and a packet of sugar.
Write a shopping list for a birthday party.

dialog.g: Hello! Can I help you?
Yes, please. Two kilos of rice and a packet of sugar.
Here you are. Anything else?
A bottle of oil and a jar of honey, please. How much is it?
It's ninety-five thousand sum.
Here you are. Thank you!

gaplar.g: The family is coming to Grandma's house.
Grandma is going to cook a lot of plov!
The milk and the meat are in the fridge.
How much rice do we need?
And is there any meat in the fridge?
But we haven't got many carrots.
Timur went to the bazaar with Dad.
Grandma cooked the plov in the biggest pot.
She added some salt and a lot of carrots, and no sugar, of course!
In the evening twenty people came.

dialog.g: Timur, we're going to make plov for twenty people!
Wow! How much rice do we need?
A lot of rice — four kilos. Look in the cupboard.
There are only two packets. And is there any meat in the fridge?
Yes, there is some meat. But we haven't got many carrots.
I'll go to the bazaar!

gaplar.g: Much, many and a lot of.
On Saturday Madina made pancakes for her family.
She needed some flour, some milk, two eggs and a little sugar.
'Yes, there's some in the fridge,' said Mum.
Madina didn't add much sugar because her grandpa doesn't like sweet food.
Her brothers ate a lot of pancakes with honey.
'You are the best cook!' they said.
Write a recipe of your family's favourite dish.
Why didn't Madina add much sugar?
Have you got a dream place to visit?
How can we get there quickly?
A plane is the fastest way to travel.
A lot of planes fly from there every day.
You need a passport to travel to other countries.
Our flight to Istanbul is at ten o'clock.
We're going to fly to London.
You'll probably sleep on the plane.
I'm going to watch the clouds!

dialog.g: Have you got your passport, Lola?
Yes, it's in my bag. When is our flight?
At ten. We're going to fly to London.
How long will the flight be?
About seven hours. You'll probably sleep on the plane.
No, I won't! I'm going to watch the clouds!

gaplar.g: We went to the station at seven o'clock in the morning.
Dad bought four tickets for the fast train Afrosiyob.
Our train is on platform two.
The journey from Tashkent to Samarkand by fast train is about two hours.
How are we going to travel?
It's the fastest train in Uzbekistan.
Hurry up, the train is coming!
Plan a journey to a city in Uzbekistan.
How are you going to travel?

dialog.g: Dad, which platform is our train on?
Platform two. Have you got your ticket?
Yes, here it is. How long is the journey?
About two hours. It's the fastest train in Uzbekistan.
Faster than a car?
Yes, much faster! Hurry up, the train is coming!
How much is a ticket to …? Which platform?

gaplar.g: We're going on a trip tomorrow!
What are we going to take with us?
Tonight I'm going to pack my suitcase.
We're going to swim in the lake!
I packed some T-shirts, two dresses and my sun hat.
Are you going to take any books?
And my English notebook — I'm going to write about the trip!

dialog.g: Madina, did you pack your suitcase?
Yes! I packed some T-shirts, two dresses and my sun hat.
Did you take a towel?
Yes, I did. And my toothbrush.
Good. Are you going to take any books?
Only one. And my English notebook — I'm going to write about the trip!

gaplar.g: It's late and we are tired.
Where are we going to sleep?
Our hotel is in the old city.
Our room is on the fifth floor.
We can see the Kalon Minaret from our window.
Can I have a room for four people?

dialog.g: Good evening! Can I help you?
Yes, please. Can I have a room for four people?
Your room is 507, on the fifth floor. Here is your key.
Is there a lift?
Yes, it's on the left. And your room has the best view in the hotel!
Wonderful! What time is breakfast?
From seven to ten.
From my window I can see … .

gaplar.g: There are a lot of numbers.
It shows the times of the trains.
My seat is number twelve, next to the window.
On the night train every seat is a bed!
Tickets are cheaper on the night train, but the journey is longer.
When does Afrosiyob arrive in Bukhara?
How can you travel on water?
On Charvak Lake you can go by boat.
A ship is bigger than a boat.
The road from Tashkent to Chimgan goes into the mountains.
In the morning there is a lot of traffic in the city.
How are we going to get there?
And on the lake we'll take a boat!

dialog.g: Let's go to Charvak on Sunday!
Good idea! How are we going to get there?
By car. The road is beautiful.
But there's always a lot of traffic on Sunday.
Then let's go early. And on the lake we'll take a boat!
Great! I'll bring the sandwiches.

gaplar.g: Khiva is far from Tashkent — about one thousand kilometres!
A lot of tourists come to Khiva every year.
The flight is about two hours.
Khiva is only thirty kilometres from the airport.
It's in the old city, Ichan Kala.
We arrived in Khiva in the evening.
Our hotel was small, but the view was wonderful — old walls and minarets!
The next morning we walked in the old city.
There were a lot of tourists from France, Japan and England.
I talked to a girl from London in English!
I climbed the Islam Khoja Minaret.
It's the tallest minaret in Khiva.

dialog.g: Dad, how are we going to travel to Khiva?
First by plane to Urgench. The flight is about two hours.
And then?
Then by taxi. Khiva is only thirty kilometres from the airport.
Did you book a hotel?
Yes, I did. It's in the old city, Ichan Kala.
How are we going to travel? — By plane.
We arrived in the evening. We walked in the old city.

gaplar.g: It left Tashkent at night and arrived in the morning.
In the morning there was a wonderful view.
Next year you'll come with me!
Choose the transport, the hotel and the time.
How did Grandpa travel to Termez?

dialog.g: Grandpa, how did you travel to Termez last month?
By train. It left Tashkent at night and arrived in the morning.
Was the journey boring?
No! I slept in my seat. In the morning there was a wonderful view.
Where did you stay?
In a small hotel near the station. Next year you'll come with me!

gaplar.g: Where do you like to go in the summer?
Uzbekistan hasn't got a sea, but it has got wonderful lakes!
Last summer we went to the beach at Charvak Lake.
The sand was hot and yellow.
The wind was strong and there were big waves on the lake.
It was very sunny, so I wore my sunglasses.
The waves were big and the water was cold.
Write four sentences about a day on the beach (real or dream).
It's yellow and hot on the beach.

dialog.g: Lola, where did you go last weekend?
We went to the beach at Charvak!
Did you swim?
Yes, I did. The waves were big and the water was cold.
What did you do on the beach?
I lay on the sand in my new sunglasses and Ali made a sand castle.

gaplar.g: Do you like sleeping outside under the stars?
Every summer Aziz goes to a summer camp in Zaamin.
At the camp the children sleep in tents.
In the evening they sit around the campfire and sing songs.
Last summer I went to a camp in Zaamin with my class.
We slept in tents in the forest.
In the evening we made a campfire, cooked potatoes and told funny stories.
One night I heard a noise.
Plan a camp for your class.
Tashkent is the biggest city in Uzbekistan.
Do you know any famous places there?
Our cousins from Fergana came to Tashkent.
He told us a lot about the city.
We visited the Amir Temur Museum.
In the square there is a statue of Amir Temur on a horse.
First we saw the statue of Amir Temur.
It was the most interesting place!

dialog.g: What did you see in Tashkent, Sardor?
We went sightseeing with a guide. First we saw the statue of Amir Temur.
Did you go to a museum?
Yes, the Amir Temur Museum. It was the most interesting place!
How did you travel in the city?
By metro! The stations are very beautiful.

gaplar.g: When you travel, what do you bring home for your family and friends?
In Rishtan I bought a blue bowl.
It's a souvenir for my mum.
There is a picture of Registan on it.
I'm going to send the postcard to my friend in Andijan.
Don't forget to put a stamp on the postcard!
We arrived on Monday by train.
The weather is very hot — forty degrees!
Yesterday we went sightseeing with a guide.
We saw the Kalon Minaret and the Ark.
Today I'm going to buy some souvenirs at the old bazaar.

dialog.g: My … bought it in … . It's from … .

gaplar.g: The flag of Uzbekistan is blue, white and green.
Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan.
London is the capital of England.
Last summer Nigora's family went abroad — to Turkey.
Nigora took a lot of photos with her new camera.
We went to Turkey by plane.
We stayed in Istanbul — the biggest city.
This is the sea and this is a Turkish flag.
Choose a country you want to visit.

dialog.g: Nigora, did you go abroad last summer?
Yes, I did! We went to Turkey by plane.
Did you visit the capital?
No, we didn't. We stayed in Istanbul — the biggest city. The capital is Ankara.
Did you take photos?
I'm going to go to … . The capital is … .

gaplar.g: Do you write about your days?
Some people write every day in a special notebook.
Lola writes in her diary every evening.
The view from the mountain was amazing!
My best memory of the summer is the trip to Khiva.
We went for a long walk.
We stayed in the hotel, played chess and relaxed.
Chimgan is famous for its mountains.
We went up the mountain by cable car.
Last July Nigora and her family went to Chimgan for a week.
They stayed in a small hotel near the mountains.
On the first day they went up the mountain by cable car.
She took a lot of photos with her new camera.
I took a photo of a flag there.
This is my best memory — and my worst too!

dialog.g: Oh no! Where's my camera? I lost it!
When did you see it last?
At the top of the mountain. I took a photo of a flag there.
Let's go to the cable car station and ask.
Is this your camera? A tourist found it.
Yes! Thank you! This is my best memory — and my worst too!
went, took, lost, found
When did you see it? the best, the worst, amazing

gaplar.g: I bought a postcard and sent it to my grandma.
Write a holiday story in six sentences.
What did Madina send to her grandma?

dialog.g: Aziz, where did you go last summer?
I went to a camp. We slept in tents.
And you, Madina?
I went abroad, to Russia. I visited the capital, Moscow.
Did you buy any souvenirs?
Yes, I did. I bought a postcard and sent it to my grandma.
went, stayed, saw, bought, amazing, memory.

gaplar.g: We learned a lot this year!
Let's travel through all the year — from the funny monkey to Nigora's camera.
Dear class, This year was amazing!
The winner gets a 'prize' — a big clap!
When did the class cook plov?
Where is Lola going to travel?

dialog.g: I'm going to visit my aunt.

gaplar.g: It's the last English lesson of the year!
Our favourite words What are the best words of the year?

dialog.g: Look! A time machine! Let's press the button!
Where are we? It's the year 2080!
Hello! I'm Robi. I'll show you the future. People will live on Mars!
Wow! Can we go back now? I'm hungry.
OK, press the button again… We're home! Mum made plov!
Plov is the best food in the past, now and in the future!

gaplar.g: What did you do in the summer?
Last year we were in Grade 6.
There are twenty-five pupils in our class.
Last summer Ali went to Samarkand.
He saw the Registan and ate samsa.
The Registan is the most beautiful place in the city!
Next summer I'm going to visit Bukhara.

dialog.g: Where did you go in the summer, Ali?
I went to Samarkand with my family. We travelled by train.
Did you take photos?
Yes, I did. The Registan is the most beautiful place in the city!
I stayed at my grandma's house. Next summer I'm going to visit Bukhara.

gaplar.g: Every morning Aziz walks to school.
But today it is very cold.
Aziz usually goes to school on foot.
Today it is cold, so he is taking a bus.
Our teacher usually drives, but today she is taking a taxi.
Our neighbour, Mr Karimov, usually works in his garden in the morning.
Which one is about every day?

dialog.g: Good morning, Aziz! You usually walk to school. Why are you at the bus stop?
It's very cold today, so I'm taking a bus.
Good idea. I usually work in my garden, but today I'm staying at home.
Are you busy?
Yes, I'm reading a big book. Have a good day!
How do you usually go to school? How are you going home today?

gaplar.g: What do you do after school?
Some people play football, some people draw.
He has got a hundred books!
Grandpa collects stamps from different countries.
Nigora has got coins from France and England.
In my free time I read or play chess.

dialog.g: What are you doing, Timur?
I'm looking at my stamps. Collecting stamps is my hobby.
How many stamps have you got?
About three hundred. This one is from France.

gaplar.g: Madina is very busy this month.

These days I'm reading a very interesting book.
Madina practises the piano for two hours.
Madina plays the piano very well.

I'm playing in a competition next week.
But these days I'm practising every evening.

dialog.g: Madina, what are you doing these days?
I'm practising the piano. I'm playing in a competition next week.
How often do you usually practise?
Usually three times a week. But these days I'm practising every evening.
And Aziz?
He's learning the dutar these days. His grandpa is teaching him.
These days I'm … . I usually … , but these days I'm … .

gaplar.g: Our class is making something big this week.
Can you guess what it is?
This week our class is doing a project about Uzbek cities.
Lola is drawing a big poster of Samarkand.
Ali is cutting photos with scissors.
Then he puts the photos on the poster with glue.
Let's draw a map of Khiva too.

dialog.g: What are you doing, Lola?
I'm drawing the Registan for our poster.
Great! Ali, are you helping her?
Yes, I am. I'm cutting photos. Where is the glue?
It's on my desk. I have an idea! Let's write about plov too.
Good idea, Aziz. Our project is going to be the best!
We need scissors, glue and … . I have an idea: …

gaplar.g: I need scissors for my project.
It means something you like doing in your free time.
I love summer, but I hate cold winter mornings.

dialog.g: What are you doing, Madina?
I'm doing my English homework, but I don't understand this word.
Which word?
'Neighbour'. What does it mean?
Our neighbours live next to us. Mr Karimov is our neighbour.
Oh, now I understand! But I always forget new words.
Write them on small cards. It helps!

gaplar.g: Every spring we have a picnic in the park.
In this photo Grandma is smiling.
His little brother is very funny.
Dad is carrying a big pot of sumalak.
When we describe a photo, we talk about it like it is happening now.
Every year we have a picnic there at Navruz.

dialog.g: What a nice photo! Where are you?
We're in the park. Every year we have a picnic there at Navruz.
Who is that man? He's carrying something big.
That's my dad. He's carrying sumalak. We always cook it together.
And why is your brother laughing?
Grandpa is telling a funny story. He always tells funny stories!

gaplar.g: Timur is in Khiva this week with his class.
A lot of tourists visit Khiva every year.
Our guide tells us stories about the old city.
I usually get up at seven and go to school on foot.
But these days I'm not at school.
I'm in Khiva with my class!
We're staying in a small hotel.
Today our guide is showing us the old city.
It's sunny and a lot of tourists are taking photos.
Right now I'm sitting on an old wall and writing these notes.
Our words Let's say all the words from Unit 1.
Do you usually play in competitions?
But these days I'm practising every day.
Your partner guesses the false one.
He's got a hundred from different countries.

dialog.g: You look busy, Aziz. What are you doing?
I'm making a poster for the music competition. I need some glue.
Here you are. Do you usually play in competitions?
No, I usually play the dutar at home. But these days I'm practising every day.
Good luck! I know you can win.

gaplar.g: At eight o'clock, what were you doing?
Yesterday at eight o'clock I was at home.
At that time I was doing my homework.
We have dinner at seven in the evening.
After dinner Dad usually washes the dishes.
Grandma sweeps the garden every morning.
Lola was sweeping the floor in the kitchen.
And what were you doing at that time?
My dad and I were jumping and singing!

dialog.g: What were you doing yesterday at eight o'clock, Ali?
I was having dinner with my family. Why?
There was a great football match on TV!
Oh no! And what were you doing at that time?
I was watching the match, of course. My dad and I were jumping and singing!

gaplar.g: Is it sunny or rainy today?
Our story today is about a rainy day.
While Mum was cooking, I was doing my homework.
Yesterday there was a lot of rain in Tashkent.
I always take my umbrella in autumn.
I didn't have an umbrella, so my clothes were wet.
Little Timur was jumping in the puddles!
While we were talking, I forgot to take it back.
Make one sentence Join two long actions with while.
Describe Think about a rainy day.

dialog.g: Madina, why are you so wet?
It was raining while I was walking home from school.
Where was your umbrella?
Nigora had it. While we were talking, I forgot to take it back.
And your shoes? They're very wet too!
Little Timur was jumping in the puddles, and I was holding his hand!
While I was … , it was raining.

gaplar.g: My phone is in my bag.
Yesterday my phone rang three times.
I was doing my homework when the phone rang.
While I was talking to her, somebody knocked on the door.
And suddenly the doorbell rang too.

dialog.g: Why didn't you come to the park yesterday?
Oh, it was a funny evening! I was doing my homework when the phone rang.
Who was it?
It was Grandma. While I was talking to her, somebody knocked on the door.
And then?

gaplar.g: What can we say when a friend falls?
Yesterday Aziz fell off his bike.
I fell and hurt my knee.
The floor was wet and Madina slipped.
I hurt it in the football match.
Timur fell and hurt his knee.

dialog.g: Timur! What happened to your knee?
I fell in the school garden.
How did it happen?
I was running in the rain when I slipped. The grass was very wet.
Does it hurt?
Yes, a little.
Let's go and see the school doctor. And no running in the rain next time!

gaplar.g: Somebody took a beautiful necklace from a shop last night.
A detective asks a lot of questions.
The thief ran out of the shop.
Grandma has got a beautiful old necklace.
The guard was sleeping at that time.
Where were you at nine o'clock?
But at nine my phone rang, and I was talking for ten minutes.
The thief came in while you were talking.
Short answers Answer with was or were only.
Detective game One pupil is the detective.

dialog.g: Somebody stole a necklace last night. Where were you at nine o'clock?
I was here, in the shop.
What were you doing?
I was walking around and checking the doors.
Were you sleeping?
No, I wasn't! But at nine my phone rang, and I was talking for ten minutes.
Ten minutes! The thief came in while you were talking.

gaplar.g: Good stories often start with the weather.
The sun was shining and the sky was blue.
There was a big storm last night.
My cat is scared of it.
We saw lightning in the dark sky.
Stories often start with a picture.
Last summer we were camping in the mountains.

dialog.g: The sun was shining. Birds were singing.
We heard thunder. We ran into the tent.

gaplar.g: Ulugbek built an observatory in Samarkand.
At night we can see a lot of stars.
One night in 1437 the sky over Samarkand was dark.

Suddenly a young student ran in.
He wrote the star's place in his book.

dialog.g: What was Ulugbek doing? What were his students doing? What happened suddenly?

Last night there was a storm. I was sleeping when I heard loud thunder.
Were you scared?
A little. While the wind was blowing, my little brother was crying.
And then?
Suddenly the lights went off. Dad found his phone and we used its light.

gaplar.g: What are the rules in our school?
Are they a choice, or are they very important?
You're wearing one, so that's fine.
And you must do your homework every day!
Questions with must We can ask about rules with must, too.
Our class rules In groups, write five rules for your classroom with must.

dialog.g: It's my first day here. What are the rules?
Well, we must wear a uniform. You're wearing one, so that's fine.
What time must I come?
Lessons start at eight. You must come on time.
Anything else?
You must be polite to teachers and pupils. And you must do your homework every day!

gaplar.g: Some things are dangerous or bad at school.
You mustn't run in the corridor.
Our classroom is at the end of the long corridor.
You mustn't eat chewing gum in class.
You mustn't cheat in a test.

dialog.g: Aziz! Ali! Stop! You mustn't run in the corridor.
Sorry, teacher. We're late for the music lesson.
You can fall and hurt your knee. Walk, please. Ali, what are you eating?
Chewing gum.
You mustn't eat chewing gum at school. Take it out, please.
OK. Sorry!

gaplar.g: At home there are rules too.
Who makes the bed in your family?
I have to get up at seven on school days.
On Sunday I don't have to get up early.
Everyone in my family helps with the housework.
Every morning I make my bed.
Grandma waters the flowers in the evening.
I have to make my bed and water the flowers every day.

dialog.g: I have to get up at seven.
Do you have to help with the housework, Aziz?
Yes, I do. I have to make my bed and water the flowers every day.
Does your sister have to wash the dishes?
Yes, she has to wash them after dinner. And you?

gaplar.g: This week our class is visiting a museum in Tashkent.
We are allowed to take photos, but we aren't allowed to touch things.
There are old coins and clothes in the history museum.
Let's meet at the entrance of the museum at ten.
After the visit we left through the exit.
Please read the sign at the entrance.
But you aren't allowed to touch the old things.
There is a café near the exit.

dialog.g: Welcome to the museum! Please read the sign at the entrance.
Are we allowed to take photos?
Yes, you are. But you aren't allowed to touch the old things.
Are we allowed to eat here? I'm hungry!
No, you aren't. There is a café near the exit.

gaplar.g: Aziz is always tired at school.
Let's help him with some advice.
My grandma always gives me good advice.
You shouldn't eat a lot of sweets.
They are bad for your teeth.
Chips and burgers are junk food.
Run, swim or ride a bike!
You should sleep enough — nine hours every night.
What time do you go to bed?

dialog.g: You look tired, Aziz. What time do you go to bed?
At about twelve. I play games on my phone.
That's very late. You should go to bed at ten. You need enough sleep.
What else?
You shouldn't eat junk food in the evening, and you should do some exercise every day.
Thank you for the advice!

gaplar.g: Do you go to a club after school?
Timur goes to a chess club on Tuesdays.
There are twenty members in our bike club.
Our coach helps us to ride faster.
You must wear a helmet when you ride a bike.
Wear a helmet and be safe on the road!
We only ride in the park.
Choose the best word Which word fits?

dialog.g: I want to be a member of the bike club. What are the rules?
You must wear a helmet. It keeps you safe.
Do I have to bring my bike?
No, you don't have to. The club has bikes. But you should bring water.
Are we allowed to ride on the road?
No, you mustn't ride on the road. We only ride in the park.

gaplar.g: Bobur is new at our school.

No, you aren't. And you mustn't take your phone to bed!

gaplar.g: Some people never leave their city.
Have you ever been to Bukhara?

I have been to the sea once — last summer.

dialog.g: Have you ever been to Bukhara, Lola?
Yes, I have. I've been there twice. And you?
No, I haven't. But I've been to Samarkand once.
Have you ever been abroad?
No, never. Have you?
Yes, I've been to Russia with my parents.

gaplar.g: I have seen the Registan at night.
Have you ever met a famous person?

An eagle is a big bird.

dialog.g: Have you ever been to Chimgan, Nigora?
Yes, I have. I've seen a waterfall there. It was great!
Have you ever seen a wild animal?

gaplar.g: Uzbek food is famous in the world.

Have you ever flown in a plane?
Have you ever ridden a camel?

dialog.g: Madina, have you ever tried Korean food?
Yes, twice. We flew to Moscow last year. Have you?

Wow! I've never ridden a camel. Was it scary?
A little, but it was fun.

gaplar.g: Tomorrow Lola's family is going to Bukhara by train.

He's just come back from the station.

Lola, have you packed your bag?

I want to talk to him.

It is hard to breathe in dirty air.
There is a lot of traffic, and cars make smoke.
These days the air is getting dirtier.
Then we can breathe clean air.

dialog.g: Grandpa, why is the sky grey today?
Because of pollution. There is a lot of traffic, and cars make smoke.
Was the air clean when you were young?
Yes, it was. There weren't many cars. These days the air is getting dirtier.
What should we do?
We should walk or ride bikes more. Then we can breathe clean air.

gaplar.g: How many plastic bags does your family use every week?
Please don't leave rubbish in the park.
Plastic bags stay in nature for hundreds of years.
Put your rubbish in the bin, please.
I always take a water bottle to school.
We throw away a lot of plastic every day.
Somebody has left rubbish under the tree.

dialog.g: Timur, look! Somebody has left rubbish under the tree.
Plastic bottles and bags again! That's bad.
Where is the bin?
It's near the entrance. Let's take the bottles there.
People shouldn't throw away rubbish in parks. Animals can eat plastic!
You're right. I've already found three bottles!

gaplar.g: Old paper can become a new notebook.
An old bottle can become a T-shirt!
We recycle paper, glass and plastic.
Glass bottles go into the green bin.
Put old paper in the blue bin.
Tin cans go into the yellow bin.
I reuse old boxes for my toys.
Our school has started a recycling project.
Every Friday a big car takes the rubbish to a recycling centre.
There, old paper becomes new notebooks, and plastic bottles become T-shirts and bags.
We can save energy at home and at school.
Cars, lights and computers need energy.
Turn off the light when you leave the room.
The TV and the fridge use electricity.
Turn off the tap when you brush your teeth.
And the TV is on, but nobody is watching it.
He was brushing his teeth while he was singing!
Energy detective Walk around your home tonight.
What is on, but nobody is using it?

dialog.g: Lola, you've left the light on in your room again!
Sorry, Dad. I forgot.
We should save electricity. And the TV is on, but nobody is watching it.
OK, I'll turn it off.
And who left the tap on in the bathroom?
That was my little brother! He was brushing his teeth while he was singing!

gaplar.g: Most of the Aral Sea has disappeared.
The land around the sea is very dry now.
Old ships are standing in the desert.
The wind carries a lot of dust from the dry sea.
He caught a lot of fish in the Aral Sea.
In 1960 the Aral Sea was a big blue lake.
Fishermen were working on their ships every day.
Then people took too much water from the rivers for their fields.
Year after year the sea got smaller.
Now most of it has disappeared.

dialog.g: what happened and what we should do.

gaplar.g: Last Saturday Nigora's school club had a big day.
On Saturday there was a big clean-up in our park.
We wore gloves to collect the rubbish.
Last Saturday our club had a clean-up day by the river.
We wore gloves and collected plastic bottles, bags and tin cans.
While we were working, a fisherman came and helped us.
Now the river is clean, and we have put three new bins there.
Next month we are going to plant trees.
Find the times Find one example of each time in the story.
Our words Let's put the Unit 5 words into groups.
The green bin is for glass.
You're a real eco detective, Madina.
Eco quiz In groups, make three quiz questions about the environment for another group.
What has happened to the Aral Sea?
Which word is about water at home?
Let's protect our planet every day!

dialog.g: Aziz, what did you throw in the bin?
An old glass bottle.
You shouldn't put glass in that bin! It's for paper. The green bin is for glass.
Oh, sorry. I didn't know.
And you have left the classroom light on again!
I'm turning it off now! You're a real eco detective, Madina.

gaplar.g: How many hours do you watch TV every day?
What do you like to watch?
My dad watches the news every evening at nine.
There are a lot of cartoons on this channel.
My little sister watches cartoons every morning.
The presenter tells us the news.
I always watch the news at nine.
But right now I'm watching my favourite presenter.
Compare a habit and this moment.

dialog.g: Grandma, how often do you watch TV?
Every day. I always watch the news at nine.
Which channel do you like?
I like the history channel. Its programmes are very interesting.
Do you ever watch cartoons?
Sometimes — with your little brother! But right now I'm watching my favourite presenter. Shh!

gaplar.g: Can you live without the internet for one day?
Let's talk about how we use it.
We use the internet every day.
I sometimes do my homework online.
Our school has a website with news and photos.
I search for information on the internet.
My sister does her project on her laptop.
It has a lot of photos.
My mum says I shouldn't stay online too long.
Online phrases Learn these phrases together.
How long do you stay online every day?
Say how you can find information.
How often do you watch the news?

dialog.g: What are you doing on your laptop, Madina?
I'm searching for information about the Aral Sea for my project.
Have you found a good website yet?
Yes, I've just found one. It has a lot of photos.
How often do you go online?
Every day, but only for an hour. My mum says I shouldn't stay online too long.

gaplar.g: A lot of young people make videos and write blogs.
Do you know any Uzbek bloggers?
Timur makes funny videos about his cat.
Lola writes a blog about Uzbek food.
She posts a new photo every week.
My friends write nice comments under my videos.
Can you share the video with me?
Every week, these days or now?
My cat was sleeping when the phone rang, and she jumped!
Can I share it with my sister?
I post a new video every Saturday.
Plan a blog Plan your own blog.

dialog.g: Timur, I've just watched your new video. It's so funny!
Thanks! My cat was sleeping when the phone rang, and she jumped!
I've written a comment under it. Can I share it with my sister?
Of course! I post a new video every Saturday.
What are you making these days?
These days I'm making a video about our school project.

gaplar.g: The internet is useful, but it can be dangerous too.
A stranger is a person you don't know.
Your address and phone number are private.
Never write your home address online.
Children shouldn't have too much screen time.
Don't click on strange pictures or messages!
He says I've won a phone!
You did the right thing — you told me.

dialog.g: Mum, somebody has written to me online. He wants my address.
Do you know him?
No, he's a stranger. He says I've won a phone!
Don't answer, and don't click on anything. Your address is private.
OK. I've just closed the message.
Good boy. You did the right thing — you told me.

gaplar.g: Before the internet, people got news from newspapers.
Does anybody in your family still read them?
Grandpa reads the newspaper every morning with his tea.
My sister buys a magazine about animals every month.
There is an interesting article about Khiva in this magazine.
A journalist writes articles for newspapers.
There were thirty old coins in it!
'I was planting a tree,' Ali told our journalist.
People at the city museum say the coins are about 500 years old.
Ali has given them to the museum.
A good article answers these questions.
Be a journalist Interview a classmate about something interesting from last week.

dialog.g: 'Pupils clean river'

gaplar.g: How many hours do pupils in our class watch videos?
Let's do a survey and find out!
We did a survey in our class about TV and the internet.
Fifty percent of the pupils watch TV every day.
We did a fun quiz about famous Uzbek people.
We asked 25 pupils in our class about media.
Most pupils (80 percent) watch videos online every day.
Sixty percent watch cartoons or the news on TV.
Twelve pupils have written a blog, and three pupils post videos every week.
Do a survey In groups, make a survey with four questions about media.
How many pupils did they ask?
Today she is writing a special post.
Lola's blog has five hundred followers.
I usually post photos of Uzbek food every Friday.
But today I'm writing something different.
Yesterday I was cooking samsa with Grandma when the phone rang.
It was a journalist from a magazine!
She has read my blog and she wants to write an article about me.
I've never been in a magazine before!
Find the times Find the examples in the post.
Our words Let's put the Unit 6 words into groups.
I watched a programme about Navoi for my project.
Did you search for information online?
And I've just read an article in Grandpa's newspaper.
You should post your project on the school blog.
Media game Say a media word.
Your partner makes a sentence with it.

dialog.g: Aziz, how much screen time have you had today?
Only one hour, Dad. I watched a programme about Navoi for my project.
Good. Did you search for information online?
Yes, I found a very good website. And I've just read an article in Grandpa's newspaper.
Well done! You should post your project on the school blog.

gaplar.g: Ibn Sino was born in 980 near Bukhara.
A scientist studies the world and finds new things.
Ibn Sino lived in the tenth and eleventh centuries.
When and where were they born?
Ibn Sino was born in 980 in a village near Bukhara.
As a boy, he loved books and learned very fast.
At sixteen he was already treating sick people.
Ibn Sino wrote more than 200 books.
Doctors in Europe studied his book about medicine for 600 years.
Alisher Navoi was a great Uzbek poet.
We learned a short poem by Navoi at school.
Navoi wrote poems in two languages.
He became a famous poet when he was young.
Biographies use a lot of irregular past forms.
Alisher Navoi was born in 1441 in Herat.
As a child he loved poems and wrote his first poems at about ten.
Later he became a friend and helper of the king, Husayn Bayqara.
Navoi built schools, hospitals and bridges.
But most of all, he was a poet.

dialog.g: When and where was Navoi born? What did he build? In which language did he write?

gaplar.g: Ulugbek discovered many new things about the stars.
An astronomer studies stars and planets.
He was the king of Samarkand for forty years.
He was very good with numbers.
How many stars did Ulugbek study?
In which word does -ed sound like /id/?
Ulugbek discovered a lot about the stars!

dialog.g: Who was Ulugbek?
He was Amir Temur's grandson and the king of Samarkand.
What did he build?
He built a madrasah on the Registan and a big observatory.
What did he discover?
He studied more than a thousand stars and wrote their places in a book.
And he found how long a year is: 365 days and about 6 hours!

gaplar.g: Lights, phones, bikes — somebody invented all these things!
Alexander Bell invented the telephone in 1876.
Thomas Edison was a famous inventor.
The internet is a great invention.
Edison made a good light bulb in 1879.
The wheel is a very old invention.

dialog.g: Grandpa, let's play a quiz! Who invented the telephone?
Alexander Bell, of course. In 1876.
Right! What did Thomas Edison invent?
A good light bulb. Before that, people used candles.
Correct! And who invented the wheel?
Nobody knows! It's a very old invention — more than five thousand years old.

gaplar.g: Two thousand years ago a long road went from China to Europe.
It went through Samarkand and Bukhara!
An explorer travels to new places and writes about them.
Samarkand and Bukhara were big cities on the Silk Road.
Merchants carried silk, tea and paper.
Columbus sailed across the sea in 1492.
A caravan of camels was walking through the desert.
The Silk Road was a long road from China to Europe.
For hundreds of years merchants travelled on it with caravans of camels.
They carried silk, paper and tea.
Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva were rich cities on the road.
Famous explorers Read about three explorers.

dialog.g: What did merchants carry? Which cities were on the Silk Road? Why were explorers' books important?

gaplar.g: A biography tells the story of a person's life.
I'm reading a biography of Amir Temur.
Ibn Sino had a long and interesting life.
She won first prize in the competition.
Rustam Kasimdzhanov became the world chess champion in 2004.
Nodirbek Abdusattorov was born in 2004 in Tashkent.
He started to play chess when he was five.
In 2021 he became the world champion in rapid chess.
In 2022 he and his team won the Chess Olympiad for Uzbekistan.
Today he is a hero for many young players.

dialog.g: When was Nodirbek born? When did he start chess? What did he become in 2021?

gaplar.g: This year we have started algebra at school.
Muhammad al-Khwarizmi was born in about 780 in Khorezm.
As a young man he went to Baghdad, a big city of scientists.
There he worked in a famous library.
He wrote a book about a new kind of mathematics.
Its name gave us the word 'algebra'.
He also showed people how to use numbers with zero.
Today every computer uses his ideas.
The word 'algorithm' comes from his name!
Fact file Let's make a fact file.

dialog.g: al-Khwarizmi
about 780, Khorezm
in Baghdad Famous for: algebra, numbers with zero
Where was al-Khwarizmi born? Where did he work? What words come from him?
Ibn Sino, Navoi, Ulugbek or Beruni.

gaplar.g: Our words Let's put the Unit 7 words into groups.
Who wrote more than 200 books about medicine and science?
What did Ulugbek build in Samarkand?
Who became a world chess champion at seventeen?
Write Write a short biography (6 sentences) of a famous person you like.
In which word does -ed sound like /t/?

dialog.g: Welcome to our history quiz! Who wrote more than 200 books about medicine and science?
Ibn Sino!
Correct! What did Ulugbek build in Samarkand?
An observatory and a madrasah.
Right! Who became a world chess champion at seventeen?
Nodirbek Abdusattorov!
Well done! You have won the prize!

gaplar.g: Grandma has a great recipe for plov.
The ingredients for this salad are tomatoes, cucumbers and onions.
Put the tomatoes in a big bowl.
Finally, put the salad on the table.
The ingredients are tomatoes and onions.
Then cut them and the onions into small pieces.
Finally, put it next to the plov!
Telling people what to do In recipes we start with the verb.

dialog.g: Grandma, can you teach me your recipe for achichuk?
Of course. The ingredients are tomatoes and onions. That's all!
What do I do first?
First, wash the tomatoes. Then cut them and the onions into small pieces.
And after that?
After that, put everything in a bowl. Finally, put it next to the plov!

gaplar.g: What is the most famous Uzbek dish?
Let's learn how to make it.
Fry the meat in hot oil.
We need one kilo of meat for plov.
Put some oil in the pan.
Mum is frying eggs in a pan.
Why are you putting so much oil in the kazan?
When do we add the carrots?

dialog.g: Today we're cooking plov. Have you washed the rice?
Yes, I've already washed it. What should I do now?
Slice the onions, please. Be careful with the knife!
OK. Why are you putting so much oil in the kazan?
Good plov needs a lot of oil. Now I'm frying the meat.
It smells great! When do we add the carrots?
After the onions. And finally, the rice.

gaplar.g: Some food we fry, and some food we boil.
Today let's make shurpa, a hot Uzbek soup.
Then add the meat and vegetables.
Mix the flour and the eggs in a bowl.
Add a little salt to the soup.
Grandpa likes a lot of black pepper in his soup.
Eat the soup with a spoon.
Then mix it with a big spoon.
You can add pepper at the end.

dialog.g: Mum, how much water do we need for the shurpa?
Three litres. Boil the water first.
The water is boiling now! What next?
Add the meat, then two potatoes and three carrots.
How much salt?

gaplar.g: Uzbek bread is famous all over the world.
Do you know how people make it?
Mum baked a cake in the oven.
Make the dough with flour, water and salt.
We bake non in a tandoor.
It's a round, very hot oven.
There is a bakery near our house.
Last week our class visited a bakery in Samarkand.
The baker, Rustam aka, was making dough when we arrived.
First, he mixed flour, water and salt.

dialog.g: First, mix the flour. Then make the dough. (instructions)
First, the baker mixed the flour. Then he made the dough. (the past)

gaplar.g: Close your eyes and think of a lemon.
Who put so much salt in it?

dialog.g: How is the soup, Timur?
It's a bit too salty, Mum.
Oh no! And the salad?
The salad is delicious, but the tomatoes are a little sour.
Try this sauce. It's spicy!
Wow, it's very spicy! Can I have some sweet tea, please?

gaplar.g: Have you ever eaten in a restaurant?
Can I see the menu, please?
The waiter brought our food very quickly.
Can we have the bill, please?
For dessert I'd like ice cream.
I'd like plov and a salad, please.

dialog.g: Good evening! Here is the menu. Are you ready to order?
Yes. I'd like plov and a salad, please.
I'd like samsa and green tea.
Would you like a dessert?
Yes, please. Halva for me. It's sweet and delicious!
No dessert for me, thanks. Can we have the bill, please?

gaplar.g: In many families people cook sumalak all night.
Stir the soup with a big spoon.
We make sumalak from young wheat.
Every year at Navruz our neighbours and my family make sumalak together.
First, the women grow wheat for ten days.
After that, they put it in a kazan and stir it all night.
Last year I stayed with them.
While the women were stirring, they were singing songs.
In the morning the sumalak was ready.
Find in the story Find one example of each.
Our words Let's put the Unit 8 words into groups.
Then put some oil in a pan.
After that, fry the tomatoes and add three eggs.
Cooking show In groups, make your own cooking show.
One pupil is the presenter; the others ask questions.
Write Write your favourite recipe in 5–6 steps and say what it tastes like.

dialog.g: Welcome to my cooking show! Today we're making eggs with tomatoes.
First, slice two tomatoes. Then put some oil in a pan.
How much oil?
Just a little. After that, fry the tomatoes and add three eggs.
Should I mix them?
Yes, mix them with a spoon. Finally, add salt and pepper. Delicious!

gaplar.g: This is our last big review!
In autumn I started going to a chess club.
These days I'm practising for a big competition.
I have never cooked plov, but next summer I'm going to learn.
What is Aziz going to learn next summer?
Our favourite words Vote for the best words of the year!
The class explains it in English without saying it.
Have you ever tried Uzbek plov?
Our halva is sweet and delicious.
Act it out Act out the play in groups.

dialog.g: Welcome to the Silk Road Café! Here is the menu.
I've travelled from China with my caravan. I'm very hungry!
And I've just come from Europe. Have you ever tried Uzbek plov?
No, never! I'd like plov, please.
And for dessert? Our halva is sweet and delicious.
Yes, please! And after that, the bill. We must go to Samarkand!

gaplar.g: He was born in 980 and wrote famous books about medicine.
I have recently been to Khiva.
I went there two weeks ago with my family.
Have you ever been to Khiva?
I was taking photos when it suddenly started to rain.
What are you doing these days?
Which sentence is about a habit?
You don't have to bring a ball.
Your summer Tell your partner about your summer.

dialog.g: Madina! Have you ever been to Khiva?
Yes, I have, recently! I was taking photos when it suddenly started to rain.
I've never been there. What are you doing these days?
I'm practising for a chess project at the moment. And you?
I usually play football, but these days I'm reading a lot.
I went…, I have never…, I was … when … .

8-sinf.nom: Bu yerda qancha vaqtdan beri yashaysan?

gaplar.g: Timur's family has a new flat.
Today they meet the girl next door.
Do you live in the same house as five years ago?
Timur's family moved from Fergana to Tashkent last week.
She lives in the flat next door.
How long have you lived in this town?
Nigora has lived here for fourteen years.
She has lived in this house since 2012.

dialog.g: Hi! Are you our new neighbour?
Yes, I'm Timur. We moved here last week.
Nice to meet you! I'm Nigora.
How long have you lived in this house?
Since 2012. That's fourteen years — since I was born!
Wow! We lived in Fergana for ten years. Now we live here.

gaplar.g: Today Madina tells us about her friend Lola.
Madina and Lola met at kindergarten when they were four.
They went to the same primary school in Samarkand.
Madina has known Lola for ten years.
Lola and Madina help each other with homework.
I have known Lola since kindergarten.

dialog.g: have known, have been, since, for, each other.

gaplar.g: How many languages can you speak?
Today Nigora interviews our English teacher for the school newspaper.
I have studied English since Grade 1.
I have studied it for eight years.
Aziz has studied Korean for a few months only.
He lived in Paris for a few years.
I've studied German for a few years.
What happens to study, teach and speak?

dialog.g: How long have you taught English, Mr Karimov?
For twenty years — since 2006.
Which languages do you speak?
Uzbek, Russian, English and a little German. I've studied German for a few years.
Do you speak it fluently?
Not yet! But I practise every day.

gaplar.g: Have you seen the old doors in Khiva?
Doors, tables and pencils come from wood.
There is a small workshop next to Rustam aka's house.
He makes beautiful doors and boxes.
He has worked in this workshop since 1985.
He has learned from the master for two years.
I was his apprentice for ten years.
He has worked with me since last spring.
Does Bobur still work with him?

dialog.g: How long have you worked in this workshop?
Since 1985. That's forty-one years!
Who taught you?
My father. I was his apprentice for ten years.
Do you have an apprentice now?
Yes, Bobur. He has worked with me since last spring.
How long have you worked here? Who taught you? Do you have an apprentice?

gaplar.g: Do you collect anything — coins, photos, postcards?
Timur's grandpa has a very big hobby.
Samarkand has been a city for more than twenty-five centuries.
Grandpa has collected stamps for five decades — that's fifty years!
Grandpa's collection has about three thousand stamps.
I have collected 120 stamps so far.
And this one is a century old!
Can I start a collection too?
Here are ten stamps — your first ones!

dialog.g: Grandpa, how long have you collected stamps?
For five decades — since 1976.
How many stamps have you got so far?
About three thousand. And this one is a century old!
Wow! Can I start a collection too?
Of course. Here are ten stamps — your first ones!

gaplar.g: Lola has a friend in England.
They don't meet, but they write to each other.
She lives in York, in England.
Lola writes an email to Emma every month.
Lola is happy when she hears from Emma.
I haven't seen my cousin for ages — since last summer!
Emma has lived in York all her life.
Dear Lola, I haven't heard from you for ages!
She has a very special job.
Aziz is proud of his grandma.
My grandma Saodat lives in Margilan.
She has lived there all her life.
She has taught maths to grandparents, parents and children from one family.
She has known some of her students for decades.
'I have had about two thousand students so far,' she says.
I am very proud of her.
Which words after them tell us 'how long'?
How long has she worked at School 5?

dialog.g: Aziz's grandma lives in Margilan. She has…

gaplar.g: How long have you taught at our school?
I lived in Bukhara for twenty-five years.
But I speak only three fluently!
Then write 5 sentences with for, since and so far.

dialog.g: Our guest today is Mr Karimov. How long have you taught at our school?
Since 2006. That's twenty years!
Have you lived in this town all your life?
No. I moved here in 2005. I lived in Bukhara for twenty-five years.
How many languages have you studied so far?
Four. But I speak only three fluently!

gaplar.g: Our class is going to Chimgan tomorrow.
In summer we often play outdoors in the park.
In winter we usually play chess indoors.
I didn't have an umbrella, so I was wet.
If it rains, we will stay indoors.
If I take it, I won't get wet!
Which form is in the other half?
Do we say 'If it will rain'?

dialog.g: Tomorrow we're going to Chimgan by bus.
What will we do if it rains?
If it rains, we will play games indoors at the hotel.
And if it's sunny?
If it's sunny, we'll walk in the mountains.
I'll take my umbrella. If I take it, I won't get wet!
What will you do if it rains? What will you do if it's sunny?
If it's cold tomorrow, … . If I don't take an umbrella, … . We'll eat in the garden if … .

gaplar.g: Timur has a very bad morning.
My alarm clock rings at seven o'clock.
If I don't hear my alarm clock, I'll oversleep.
If I leave home late, I'll miss the bus.
The lesson starts in five minutes.
If you hurry, you'll get to school on time.
If I go to bed late, I won't hear my alarm clock.
If I oversleep, I'll miss the bus.
If I miss the bus, I'll be late for school.
If I'm late, the teacher won't be happy.
So tonight I'll go to bed early!

dialog.g: If I don't do my homework, … . Each student adds one sentence.
If you put your alarm clock far from the bed, you'll get up.

gaplar.g: Next week there is a big English test.
We have a maths exam on Friday.
If you revise, you'll pass the exam.
If you don't revise, you'll fail the exam.
What will I do if I fail?
If I get a good mark, I'll buy you an ice cream!
What happens if we change the order?
Exam advice Give your partner three pieces of advice before an exam.

dialog.g: The exam is on Friday. What will I do if I fail?
You won't fail if you revise every day.
But I've revised for a week, and I still forget words.
If we revise together, it will be easier. I'll ask you questions.
Great! If I get a good mark, I'll buy you an ice cream!

gaplar.g: Lola and her mum are at the station in Tashkent.
There are a lot of people.
Unless we hurry, we'll miss the train.
Unless we hurry, we won't catch the train.
Unless you hold my hand, you'll get lost.
We won't miss it unless we stop now.

dialog.g: Hurry, Lola! Unless we hurry, we won't catch the train.
It's so crowded! Where is our train?
Platform 2. Be careful! Unless you hold my hand, you'll get lost.
Here it is! We're on time!
Phew! We won't miss it unless we stop now.

gaplar.g: Nigora is helping her grandma to make plov.
Plov is delicious, but the kitchen can be dangerous!
Grandma slices the carrots with a big knife.
If you play with a knife, you'll hurt your hand.
If you touch the hot pan, you'll burn your fingers.
But be careful — the knife is sharp.
If I go slowly, I won't hurt myself.
If you touch it, you'll burn yourself.

dialog.g: First, slice the onions. But be careful — the knife is sharp.
I know, Grandma. If I go slowly, I won't hurt myself.
Good. Now don't touch the pan. If you touch it, you'll burn yourself.
When will the plov be ready?
In an hour. Unless you open the pot every minute!

gaplar.g: Aziz's family is planning a day by Charvak Lake.
But first they watch the news on TV.
The weather forecast says it will be hot and sunny tomorrow.
There may be a storm in the afternoon, with strong wind and rain.
If there's a storm, we'll cancel the picnic.
Here is the weather forecast for Saturday.
In Tashkent it will be sunny and hot in the morning, about 30 degrees.
If you are going to the mountains, take warm clothes and an umbrella.
On Sunday it will be sunny everywhere.
What comes in the second half?
Where will you go if the picnic is cancelled?
Plan B Your family has a plan for Saturday.
Make Plan A (sunny) and Plan B (storm).
Lola has big exams at the end of the year.
She writes to her pen friend Emma about her plans.
Dear Emma, my exams start next month and I'm a bit nervous.
If I pass them, Dad will take us to Khiva in June!

Are the cars made by robots or by people? Mr
Both! The body is made by robots. The seats are put in by workers.

In the play, how did people send letters in 1950?

dialog.g: Welcome to 2026, Grandpa!

gaplar.g: A new school year has started!
