He has studied hard since September.
She used to be shy, but now she speaks English in every lesson.
I haven't seen you since June.
My uncle has a farm where cotton is grown.
If you come with me next summer, you will love it!
Which one tells us how long?
Which one is about an old habit?
Which one is about a possible future?

dialog.g: Aziz! I haven't seen you since June. Where have you been?
I've been in Fergana for two months. My uncle has a farm where cotton is grown.
That's a real achievement! What did you do there?
I have…, I used to…, If…, I will…

gaplar.g: Imagine that you have a million dollars.
What would you do with all that money?
He has three houses and five cars.
Some families in the world are poor.
Nigora always shares her lunch with her classmates.
I would travel around the world.
Nobody would be hungry in our mahalla.
And what would you do, Ali?
Maybe I would build a football stadium for our school, too.

dialog.g: If I had a million dollars, I would buy a fast car.
Really? I wouldn't buy a car. I would travel around the world.
I would share my money with poor families. Nobody would be hungry in our mahalla.
That's kind, Timur! And what would you do, Ali?
Hmm… Maybe I would build a football stadium for our school, too.
If I have time, I will help you.
If I had a million, I would buy an island. I'd = I would wouldn't = would not

gaplar.g: Sometimes our friends have problems and ask us what to do.
If I were a bird, I would fly over the mountains.
Aziz is nervous before his exam.
An honest person always tells the truth.
Can you give me some advice?
I broke my sister's phone, and she doesn't know.
If I were you, I would tell her the truth.
But if you were honest, she would trust you more.
I would apologise and help her to repair it.
I'm nervous, but I'll talk to her tonight.
In imagined situations we often use 'were' for I, he, she and it.

dialog.g: Madina, I need your advice. I broke my sister's phone, and she doesn't know.
Oh no! If I were you, I would tell her the truth.
But she will be so angry!
You're right. I'm nervous, but I'll talk to her tonight.

gaplar.g: Many films are about heroes with special powers.
Which power would you like to have?
If I were invisible, nobody would see me.
If I could speak ten languages, I would work all over the world.
The magician said a magic word, and the rabbit disappeared!
If I were invisible, I could walk into the cinema for free!
If I had a superpower, I would want to fly.
I could visit my grandma in Khiva every day.
If I were very strong, I could help people after earthquakes.
And if you could disappear for a day, where would you go?

dialog.g: Which superpower would you want, Aziz?
I'd want super strength. If I were very strong, I could help people after earthquakes.
Great ideas! And if you could disappear for a day, where would you go?

gaplar.g: In the morning you wake up on a small island in the sea.
Imagine a small island with palm trees and no people.
You can take only three things.
People can't survive for long without water.
With a knife you could cut fruit and wood.
In our English class, we played the island game.
The teacher said, 'Imagine you are on a desert island.
'If I had a knife, I could cut wood,' she said.
'If there were no battery, it would be useless,' laughed Lola.
We can start with the 'if' part or with the 'would' part.
What would you change in your town?
The mayor decides many important things for the city.
There is a lot of traffic in the city centre in the morning.
Pedestrians are people who walk in the street.
In summer children play near the fountain in the park.
Amir Temur Square is in the centre of Tashkent.
If there were more buses, there would be less traffic.
But would the shops be happy?
If more people walked there, the shops would sell more.
Where does 'would' go in a question?
What do we say in a short answer?
If there were less traffic, the air would be cleaner.
If the air were cleaner, people would be healthier.

dialog.g: If I were the mayor, I would plant more trees. The air would be cleaner.
I wouldn't build new roads. If there were more buses, there would be less traffic.
Nice! But would the shops be happy?
Of course they would! If more people walked there, the shops would sell more.

gaplar.g: How does English grammar show the difference?
Millions of people buy lottery tickets, but very few win.
Lola won first prize in the drawing competition.
If I had one, I could watch the stars every night.
Which situation does Aziz think is possible?

dialog.g: What will you do if you pass the exam next month?
And what would you do if you won the lottery?
I'd buy a telescope. If I had one, I could watch the stars every night.
If I pass the exam, I will go to camp.

gaplar.g: It is about a rich man, a poor farmer and a wise old man.
My grandfather is a wise man.
He knows the answer to every difficult question.
Long ago in Bukhara, a rich man lived next to a poor farmer.
The rich man was never happy.
In the story, people talk about imagined situations.
The story shows that money doesn't always make people happy.
Retell Retell the story in five sentences.

dialog.g: rich, poor, wise, would, share.

gaplar.g: If I could fly, I would visit Khiva.
If I were you, I would apologise.
Pedestrians would enjoy the fountain and the trees.
Which word means 'people who walk in the street'?

dialog.g: I'd close the main square to cars. Pedestrians would enjoy the fountain and the trees.
Interesting! And you, Aziz?
If I were the mayor, I'd give free buses to students. There would be less traffic.
And would you share your salary with the city?
Of course I would! But only for one day!

gaplar.g: When we tell other people what someone said, we change the words a little.
Aziz mentioned his new bike, but he didn't show it to us.
I'm at work late today, and my car doesn't start.
She said that she was tired.
She also mentioned that her car didn't start.
Compare Mum's words with Lola's report.

dialog.g: Did she say anything else?
She said she was at work late. She also mentioned that her car didn't start.
Then I'll go and pick her up. Thanks for explaining, Lola!
'I like chess.'
'I'm hungry.'
'We are late.'

gaplar.g: 'Say' and 'tell' have similar meanings, but they work differently in a sentence.
Our neighbours often complain about loud music at night.
I sent Lola a message, but she didn't reply.
I said that I was busy, not angry.
And Aziz said that you didn't want to play football with us.
I told Aziz that I had a cold.
Let's reply to Aziz together and tell him the truth.
Which verb needs a person (me, him, Aziz) after it?
Reporting promises 'I will help you.' → He promised (that) he would help me.
'I won't be late.' → She promised she wouldn't be late.
Pair work A says three sentences about yesterday.

dialog.g: Madina told me that you were angry with me. Is it true?
No! I said that I was busy, not angry.
Oh! And Aziz said that you didn't want to play football with us.
That's just gossip. I told Aziz that I had a cold.
Sorry! I promise I won't listen to gossip again.
OK. Let's reply to Aziz together and tell him the truth.

gaplar.g: Uzbekistan has many young sports stars.
A journalist writes articles for newspapers and websites.
Shahzoda is the school chess champion.
She won every game this year.
Sixteen teams played in the football tournament.
My opponent was very strong, but I won the game.
Last week, 15-year-old Javohir won the national chess tournament.
He told our journalist that he trained four hours every day.
He said that his grandfather was his first teacher.
When we asked about his opponents, he said they were very strong.
He also promised that he would play for Uzbekistan one day.
I will play for Uzbekistan.' Find them in the article.
Every day the news tells us what other people said.
Reporters use special verbs for this.
The TV channels reported that the new metro station was open.
The director announced that there would be no classes on Friday.
According to the weather forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.
After heavy rain, there was a flood in the village.
The mayor of Denov announced that schools were closed for the day.
According to the police, two roads were under water, but nobody was hurt.
Volunteers said they were helping families near the river.
The mayor told journalists that the city would repair the roads by Monday.
Find the reporting verbs in the news.
Words like 'today', 'here' and 'this' depend on when and where we speak.
What happens to them when we report words later?
The day before, she was in Samarkand.
Grandma can't type quickly, so she sends voice messages.
He said he was at the stadium then.
Aziz spoke on Monday at the stadium.

dialog.g: What else did he say?
So you missed the game. Call him and explain!

gaplar.g: Storytellers and reporters don't only use 'said'.
Other verbs show how a person spoke.
The doctor warned that too much sugar was bad for our teeth.
Ali denied that he ate the last piece of cake.
My brother claims that he can run ten kilometres in thirty minutes.
Mum insisted that it was too cold for a T-shirt.
I was doing my homework all evening!
He insisted that he was doing his homework.
Each verb tells us more than 'said'.

dialog.g: Someone ate the samsa for our guests!
It wasn't me, Grandma! Aziz was in the kitchen.

gaplar.g: Today's story happens at Chorsu Bazaar in Tashkent.
Something goes missing, and many people say different things.
A witness is a person who saw what happened.
On Saturday Madina went to Chorsu Bazaar with her aunt.
While they were buying apricots, Madina's phone disappeared from her bag.
Another witness, an old woman, insisted that the boy ran towards the bread stalls.
The officer promised he would check the cameras.
Half an hour later, a boy in a red cap came back.
Madina thanked him and apologised for the misunderstanding.
Find the reported sentences in the story.
Reporter game Interview a classmate about their weekend (three questions).
Then present the 'news' to the class with said, told, explained and promised.
Write Write a news article (6–8 sentences) for your school website.
Include a headline and at least four reporting verbs.

dialog.g: This is School Radio. Here is today's news.
This morning the director announced that the school concert would be on Friday.
Our music teacher told us that the pupils were practising every day.
Timur claimed that he was the best singer in Grade 9, but his classmates denied it!

gaplar.g: Have you ever run to catch a bus and seen it drive away?
We arrived at the station at twenty-five to ten.
The train to Samarkand leaves from platform 2.
We rushed to the station because we were late.
According to the timetable, the Afrosiyob train leaves at half past nine.
We got up late and rushed to the station.
When we arrived on the platform, the train had already left!
We arrived in Samarkand two hours later.
When we arrived, the train had left — it wasn't there any more.
One small word, 'had', changes the picture!
Timeline Draw a timeline of your morning.

dialog.g: How was your trip to Samarkand on Sunday?
Terrible at first! We got up late and rushed to the station.
Did you catch the train?
Oh no! What did you do?

gaplar.g: Sometimes we come too late and miss the best part of an event.
By the time we got to the shop, it had closed.
There was a long queue at the ticket office.
After the marathon, the runners were exhausted.
The opening ceremony of the tournament was very beautiful.
Last March my family went to the Navruz celebration in the city park.
After we had eaten some sumalak, everyone felt better.
Before we went home, we watched a show by young dutar players.
In the end, it was a great day!
Which action came first in each sentence?
Which sentence uses the past perfect, and which doesn't need it?
From the top of the mountain, the view was beautiful.
Our trip to Chimgan was unforgettable.
Don't stand too close to the edge of the roof!
Last summer Madina flew to Turkey with her parents.
She had never been on a plane before, so she was nervous.
When they arrived at the hotel, she ran to the window.
She had never seen the sea before!
Compare her words with a sentence about life until now.
Write Write about an unforgettable day (5 sentences).
'I have never been to Khiva.' — never until when?
Sherlock Holmes is a famous detective from London.
I always lock the door when I leave the house.
Someone tried to steal my bike, but the lock was too strong.
The thief ran away with a bag full of money.
There were big footprints in the snow near the house.
The thief had stolen an old gold coin from the Silk Road room.
The thief had worn sports shoes.
So the thief was a child?
The detective asks about things before the guard came.
The coin isn't here → the thief had stolen it.

dialog.g: What did you see when you came to the museum this morning?
When I arrived, somebody had broken the lock on the back door.
Had they taken anything?
Yes, they had. The thief had stolen an old gold coin from the Silk Road room.
A school bag? So the thief was a child?
'When I arrived at the museum, …'

gaplar.g: Long before planes and trains, people crossed Central Asia with camels.
Amir Temur built a big empire.
Trade between China and Europe went through our cities.
A merchant buys and sells things in different countries.
A caravan of fifty camels arrived in Bukhara.
Merchants had brought silk and paper from China and glass from the West.
By the time he died in 1405, they had built beautiful mosques, gardens and markets.
Find 'By + date' and 'by the time' in the text.
What form of the verb comes after them?
Write Imagine you are a merchant in a caravan in 1400.
Have you ever had a morning when everything went wrong?
My alarm clock rings at seven every morning.
I overslept and missed the first lesson.
I burnt the eggs because I was reading messages.
Timur spilled his tea on his homework.
When I got to the kitchen, my sister had eaten all the bread.
I made eggs, but I burnt them because I was reading messages.
Then I spilled tea on my shirt.
By the time I arrived at school, the first lesson had already started.
And then I realised that I had left my homework at home!
Which sentence means that dinner was ready when I came home?
Have you ever had a surprise party?
Today's story is about Nigora's birthday.
Ali pretended that he was asleep, but his eyes were open.
Nigora's birthday was on Friday, but nobody had said anything to her all day.
Her friends had pretended that they had forgotten.
When she came home, the flat was dark and quiet.
Mum had told her that she would be late.
Aziz had made a big cake, and Lola had decorated the room.
Nigora realised that it was the best birthday she had ever had.
Real order In the story, the events are not in the real order.
When I came, they left — at the same time.
When I came, they had left — before I came.
After / before show the order, so past simple is also OK there.
By the time we got to the airport, the queue was enormous.
When we got to the gate, they had already closed it.
In the end, it was unforgettable!
Interview Ask your partner about their most unforgettable journey.
Why did Timur's family stay with Dad's friend?

dialog.g: Today Timur tells us about his worst journey. What happened, Timur?
Did you miss the plane?
Lucky you! And the hotel?
What had you done before…? By the time you arrived, had…?

gaplar.g: Everybody has favourite activities and things they really don't like.
I can't stand waiting in long queues.
Timur is keen on taking photos of old buildings.
In my spare time I play the dutar.
On Sundays I help my grandma make plov.
I don't mind training in the rain, but I hate losing!
What do all these verbs have at the end?

dialog.g: Lola, what do you enjoy doing in your spare time?
I enjoy cooking. On Sundays I help my grandma make plov.
Is there anything you can't stand?
I can't stand getting up early at the weekend!
And you, Aziz?
I'm keen on playing basketball. I don't mind training in the rain, but I hate losing!

gaplar.g: Big goals need decisions and hard work.
After a long talk, we decided to go to Bukhara by train.
I hope to visit London one day.
We couldn't afford to buy it.
The test was difficult, but I managed to finish it on time.
Timur wanted to learn programming, so he needed a laptop.
But his family couldn't afford to buy a new one.
Timur decided to earn the money himself.
It wasn't easy, but after eight months he managed to save enough.
'I hope to make my own app next year,' he says.
'And I want to help other kids to start programming, too.'
In the text, find the verbs after wanted, decided, planned, managed and hope.
Doctors say that small daily habits can change our health.
Let's read some advice from a school doctor.
Try to avoid eating late at night.
I don't mind walking to school.
Chips and burgers are junk food.
A fizzy drink has a lot of sugar in it.
Keep on practising, and you will get better.

dialog.g: Doctor, I'm always tired in the afternoon. What should I do?
First, avoid drinking fizzy drinks. They have too much sugar. Do you mind drinking water instead?
No, I don't mind. But I really like chips!
OK. Would you mind writing it down for me?
Of course not. Here you are!

gaplar.g: The little boy refused to eat his soup.
Our neighbour offered to drive us to the airport.
Lola persuaded her dad to buy a puppy.
You need your parents' permission to go on the school trip.
Our class wanted to go camping in Zaamin for two days.
At first, the director refused to give us permission.
He said it was too far.
Then our teacher, Mrs Rahimova, offered to go with us.
Madina's father agreed to drive the bus.
We wrote a plan and promised to keep the camp clean.
Finally, we persuaded the director to say yes!
Now we are planning to go in May.
Many Uzbek pupils speak three languages.
How do good language learners do it?
Reading books helps you to grow your vocabulary.
'Learning a language is like training for sport,' she says.
I never tried to memorise long lists.
And making mistakes is normal — don't be afraid of speaking!'
What does it tell us — when, where or how?
Tips for learners In groups, write five tips for younger pupils.
Start each with an -ing subject or use 'by + -ing'.

dialog.g: 'For Aziz, memorising words is the hardest thing.'

gaplar.g: A family is driving from Tashkent to Fergana.
On the way, some small words change everything.
Let's stop at the next petrol station.
After the long drive, we got out of the car to stretch our legs.
Please switch off the lights when you leave the room.
Mum used the iron to make Dad's shirt smooth.
We need petrol, and we can stop to stretch our legs.
You put it on the shelf.

dialog.g: Good idea. Oh no! Did I remember to switch off the iron?
Yes, Mum. I remember seeing you switch it off. You put it on the shelf.
Phew! Thank you. Ali, stop playing on your phone and look at the mountains!
OK… I'll try to take a good photo of them.
And please don't forget to buy water!

gaplar.g: At fifteen, she still couldn't swim.
One day she decided to change.
She asked a coach to teach her.
She kept on practising three times a week.
After four months she managed to swim fifty metres.
Find all the verbs with -ing and with to in the story.
Madina's story shows that being determined matters more than talent.
Which of her decisions was the most important?
Retell Retell Madina's story in six sentences.
Use at least three -ing verbs and three 'to' verbs.
Why did Madina avoid going near water?
In this unit we talked about hobbies, healthy habits, decisions and language learning.
Let's sort our verbs one more time.
I hope to visit Seoul one day.
Reading K-pop song words helps a lot.
I don't mind practising every evening.
Don't forget to show me your first robot!
Make a true sentence about yourself with it as fast as you can.
Write Write a letter to a pen friend (8 sentences) about your hobbies and plans.
Use at least four -ing verbs and four 'to' verbs.

dialog.g: I've decided to join the robotics club. I really enjoy building things.
Cool! I'm planning to learn Korean. I hope to visit Seoul one day.
Is memorising the letters difficult?
Not really. Reading K-pop song words helps a lot. I don't mind practising every evening.
Great! Don't forget to show me your first robot!

gaplar.g: Half of Grade 9 is behind us!
He told me he had decided to stop eating junk food.
In September I decided to join the school newspaper.
My first job was an interview with our chess champion.
I enjoyed writing the article, but I can't stand waiting for the teacher's corrections!
Last month our class persuaded the director to let us plan a Navruz concert.
If I had more spare time, I would write for the newspaper every week.
I hope to become a journalist one day.
Write your blog Write your own blog post 'My first half of Grade 9' (8–10 sentences).
What did the class persuade the director to do?
I'm certain that Lola is at home.
I can see her bike in the garden.
The owner of the café is a friendly old man.
This phone belongs to my sister.
It must be Timur's bag — he plays chess and he's number 10 in our team!
The name on the book is 'Ali K.' It must belong to Ali.

dialog.g: Someone left this bag in the classroom. Who is the owner?
Let's look for clues. There's a chess book inside.
Are you certain?
Yes! And look — Ali's glasses are in the bag. It must be his.

gaplar.g: I don't know the answer, but I can guess.
In the evening, the trees make long shadows.
The old door creaks when you open it.

dialog.g: Timur, wake up! Did you hear that? Something creaked downstairs.
It might be the wind. The kitchen window is open.
But look — there's a shadow on the wall! It could be a thief!
Hmm… It might be Grandpa. Perhaps he wanted a glass of water.

gaplar.g: At a market, a man is selling an 'old' painting very cheaply.
Is it real, or is it a trick?
Is this a genuine Samarkand carpet or a copy?
Please write your signature at the bottom of the page.
My uncle is an expert in old coins.
He can tell you their age.
This man says this is a painting by a famous artist from 1900.
A real painting like that would cost millions.
It can't be from 1900 — this kind of paint didn't exist then.

dialog.g: It can't be genuine. A real painting like that would cost millions.
But there's a signature in the corner.

gaplar.g: Sometimes we see a result and try to guess what happened before.
Today our deductions travel into the past.
I forgot my umbrella and came home soaked.
After a day on the beach, my nose was sunburnt.
Timur has a big bruise on his knee.
You must have walked home in the rain.
You must have fallen in the park.
but we won the football match!

dialog.g: Madina! You're soaked! What happened?
Guess!
Hmm… You must have walked home in the rain. Didn't you take your umbrella?
No, I didn't. And look at Aziz!
I might have slipped on the wet grass… but we won the football match!

gaplar.g: You can see something, but you're not sure what it is.
This is a close-up of a butterfly's wing.
This satellite photo shows the Aral Sea from space.
It's round and the surface has small holes.
Could it be a golf ball?

dialog.g: Here is photo number one. It's a close-up. What could it be?
It might be an orange. It's round and the surface has small holes.
No, it can't be an orange — it's too white. Could it be a golf ball?
Good guess! Now photo two. It's a satellite photo, and it's a bit blurry.
Let's zoom in. There are blue lines and green squares… They must be rivers and fields!
Correct! It's the Fergana Valley from space.

gaplar.g: Grandpa frowned when he saw the broken window.
Nigora blushed when the teacher praised her poem.
She must be late for work.
He can't be happy with this bus service!
And the girl with flowers is smiling and blushing.
or it could be her mum's birthday!
The writer doesn't know these people.
Find the clues and the deductions.
Which deductions are about now, and which are about the past?
Today's story is a school mystery.
Read carefully and try to solve it before the end!
The police suspect that the thief came through the window.
On Monday morning, Class 9B opened their classroom door.
It was empty — no desks, no chairs, nothing!
'Thieves must have come in the night,' said Aziz.
'They can't have carried thirty desks without a car,' replied Nigora.
'Someone might have come from the garden.' The pupils suspected the new guard.
Your old desks were very old, so we have bought new ones!
The 'thief' must have been the director!
She's soaked — she must have walked in the rain.
He was with me — he can't have done it.
He doesn't eat rice in the evening.
It must have been Aziz and his friends!
We were really hungry after the match!
Detective game One pupil leaves the room.

dialog.g: The big pot of plov is empty! Who ate it?
It can't have been me — I was at music school all afternoon.
And it can't have been Grandpa. He doesn't eat rice in the evening.

gaplar.g: In a few years you will choose a career.
What would you like to do?
Let's hear what some Grade 9 pupils think.
My aunt has had a long career in medicine.
She has worked as a doctor for 25 years.
Teaching is a very important profession.
The new airport in Samarkand was planned by an architect.
A programmer writes code for apps and websites.
Our dog was ill, so we took him to the vet.
What would you like to become?
Lola, what would you like to become?
I love drawing buildings, and I'd like to design a new school one day.
I enjoy solving problems, and programmers can work from anywhere.

dialog.g: Today let's talk about careers. Lola, what would you like to become?
Wonderful. Timur?
I want to be a programmer. I enjoy solving problems, and programmers can work from anywhere.
I'd like to work with animals, so I'm planning to study to be a vet.
Great choices! Each profession needs different skills.

gaplar.g: A job is not only about what you do.
It's also about money and time.
Doctors in big hospitals usually have a good salary.
My brother earns money by giving maths lessons.
My mum works full-time, from nine to six, five days a week.
Many students have part-time jobs in cafés at the weekend.
Finding a job starts with a piece of paper — or an email.
Let's see how young people apply for jobs.
Madina's sister applied for a job at a bank.
Your CV shows your education, skills and experience.
There is a vacancy for an English teacher at our school.
I saw an advertisement for a summer job on the website.
The deadline for applications is 15 May.
I am 17 years old and I speak fluent English and Russian.
I enjoy meeting people and I am good at telling stories.
I would be happy to come for an interview.

dialog.g: I look forward to hear…
name, age, languages, experience, skills.

gaplar.g: Jasur's letter was good, and now he has an interview.
What questions will the employer ask?
I have a job interview on Monday.
To be a doctor, you need special qualifications.
My employer gave me a day off for my birthday.
There were ten candidates for one job.
Lola impressed the teachers with her excellent speech.
Why do you want to be a tour guide?
